receipt.public_excerpt: Amazon expects to spend $75 billion on capital expenditure in 2024 and even more in 2025 – mostly on its cloud computing business – due to rising demand for generative AI

evidence_items.explanation: Confirms the spending part: Amazon guided to about $75B of 2024 capex, driven mainly by generative AI demand.

receipt.public_excerpt: bi-weekly estimates of AI use rate rose from 3.7% to 5.4%, with an expected rate of about 6.6% by early Fall 2024.

evidence_items.explanation: Only about 5% of US firms used AI in producing goods or services, which supports 'not happening at scale' across the economy.

evidence_items.locator: Satya Nadella prepared remarks, Microsoft 365 Copilot section

receipt.public_excerpt: All-up, nearly 70% of the Fortune 500 now use Microsoft 365 Copilot

evidence_items.explanation: Most of the largest US companies were using a generative AI product, which cuts against 'not at scale' for big enterprises.

receipt.public_excerpt: 65 percent of organisations regularly use Gen AI for at least one business function

evidence_items.explanation: A large 2024 survey reported regular generative AI use at most respondents' organizations, which points toward integration at scale.

unresolved_gaps: Amazon's final 2024 capex figure from its 10-K was not retrieved. The $75B is October 2024 guidance.
Spending by Microsoft, Google and Meta was not checked, though he cites only Amazon's figure.
Adoption measures conflict and none measures production integration at scale directly.
